summary_for_principal: Started the next piece of work after the validator: the part that actually runs a process. Before writing code, checked whether the workflow engine already in this codebase could be reused as-is. It can't be reused directly — it turns out there are two different, older, partly-built attempts at an engine already in the codebase, and they disagree with each other, so extending either would mean choosing which set of problems to inherit. Decided instead to build a new, small execution core that reuses the genuinely solid parts of the existing tooling (LangGraph, already a dependency) without touching either old attempt. This first piece adds the three permission/safety mechanisms the new format requires before anything can run: checking permission before every action, recording every attempt durably so a crash never loses track of progress, and preventing a resumed run from repeating an action that has a real-world effect (like sending something) twice. Nothing runs yet — this is the foundation the next four pieces build on.

decisions.headline: Build a new, small execution engine targeting LangGraph directly, rather than extending either of the two existing DAG-compiler paths in compiler/.
decisions.problem: Whether the new v1 process-definition format (built in WP-01) could reuse the workflow engine already in this codebase instead of needing new execution code.
options_rejected: Extend compiler/dag_parser.py + outcome_compiler.py's node-type vocabulary to match the spec's STEP/ROUTE/PARALLEL/JOIN/FOR_EACH/GATE: rejected — this path's own route-decider node defaults silently to the first route on no match (compiler/nodes/routing.py:277), the opposite of the spec's fail-closed requirement, and only its 'step' node type has any test coverage (tests/test_compile.py, tests/test_smoke.py).

Extend compiler/graph_dsl.py + graph_compiler.py's NodeDef/GraphDefinition model instead: rejected — this is a second, independent implementation of the same idea with a different node-type vocabulary and a different dict shape (from/to instead of depends_on) from the first path, and has no test coverage at all; the two paths do not even agree with each other, so picking one over the other does not remove the disagreement, and extending both doubles the cost.

Design a translation layer that maps the new spec's Process definitions into one of the two existing DAG.yaml/GRAPH.yaml shapes: rejected — this would carry both paths' gaps (routing default-first behaviour, no JOIN, no PolicyPort) forward into the new format rather than closing them, which the spec's fail-closed and permission-first rules do not allow.
decisions.cost_to_change: A full new module tree (engine/) plus five PRs of work; reversing this after PR5 lands would mean re-doing the whole work package against a different target, not a small patch.
